rv.q: Culture | Theatre Romeo and Juliet, theatre review: Not romantic or deeply moving Despite some flashes of wit and Lily James radiating a mix of innocence and enchanting vitality as Juliet, at times Kenneth Branagh's production is curiously drab Radiant: Lily James as Juliet Johan Persson Henry Hitchings 26 May 2016 COMMENTS Kenneth Branagh's...
Though it is stylish, accessible and illuminated by Lily James, it misses the passionate intensity of the tragedy.
While this production fails to do justice to the play, Timothy Sheader and Dale Rooks’ Running Wild turns a second-rate script into a joyous theatrical adventure.

cn.t: Branagh's old-fashioned production disappoints critics, lacking romance and emotional depth. Lily James earns praise for her radiant, vital Juliet, but the staging feels curiously drab and safe.
